reviews.text: In the end, though, Amsterdam is a frustrating affair, let down by its own inanity and wayward plotting.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: This film misses the mark so often, but at least the leads salvage as much as they can, along with some other elements that keep it from being among the worst films ever made.
reviews.author: Branyan Towe

reviews.text: I have to wonder how a film full of great stars and such a compelling story (on paper) could result in such an uninspiring mess, but that’s what happens when a filmmaker prioritizes star power over writing.
reviews.author: Brittany Patrice Witherspoon

reviews.text: A moralizing version of [a] great political thriller ... I suspect that sounds like an ill-advised way to spend an evening.
reviews.author: Joshua Polanski

reviews.text: Amsterdam is noise and nothing more.
reviews.author: Zach Youngs

reviews.text: David O. Russell’s latest outing is a glibly entertaining caper completely undone by its self-importance.
reviews.author: Prabhjot Bains

reviews.text: While there has been some criticism about the plot being too busy and trying to say too many things, part of Amsterdam's charm is its "everything, everywhere, all at once" vibe.
reviews.author: Mini Anthikad-Chhibber

reviews.text: Despite being based in fact, the story ends up being rather bland and the movie becomes more about being a way to spotlight the actors.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: It's not just the wonky pacing, but that it forever feels like none of it lands the way it's supposed to. It's like a song with a beautifully formed melody played over a rhythm section that can't keep even basic time.
reviews.author: Ilan Preskovsky

reviews.text: While Amsterdam was undoubtedly enjoyable to film for its many costars, the merriment doesn't quite translate to the screen. The plethora of side characters and celebrity cameos becomes confusing for a plot that is already too elaborate.
reviews.author: Matthew Creith

reviews.text: Really dug the friendship element & honestly if it wasn’t for Bale, Robbie, Washington & Joy I probably would have dipped out on the film as the direction/story itself was all held together by strings
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: David O Russell's latest - a shaggy dog mystery with a deliberate air of penny dreadfuls - could do with more straightforward narrative and fewer screwball convolutions
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: The down-your-throat optimism at the end of Amsterdam is certainly not the vehicle this film needed for any sort of entertaining climax. I've got plenty of other places to be preached to.
reviews.author: Josh Rosenberg

reviews.text: Amsterdam wastes its immensely talented cast and a hefty budget on an unconvincing script and meandering storytelling.
reviews.author: Sameen Amer

reviews.text: A disappointment of epic proportions.
reviews.author: Santanu Das

reviews.text: Amsterdam presents itself as a work of collaborative trust (thematically, but also formally, but also philosophically) so that discrete sections which threaten to strain credulity on their own, feel woven together with care and thoughtfulness.
reviews.author: Andrew Kendall

reviews.text: It’s by no means a perfect movie and has plenty of forgettable moments, but Amsterdam is certainly entertaining and that’s enough for me.
reviews.author: Jason Flatt

reviews.text: Although the production, costume, hair and makeup design are outstanding, the material never rises to the superb level of its all star cast.
reviews.author: Carla Renata

reviews.text: I wouldn’t have missed the pro-democracy speeches that overwhelm Amsterdam in the end, had they been tacked back, but despite Russell’s strenuous efforts, you actually can’t have everything.
reviews.author: Michael Atkinson

reviews.text: The nearly impossible narrative is not quick witted let alone charming enough to be in the same vein as Preston Sturges or Ernst Lubitsch.
reviews.author: Eric Marchen

reviews.text: A kooky piece of messy Americana, but it’s enjoyable enough to make you appreciate the cast and craft.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: It looks beautiful and Daniel Pemberton ("Motherless Brooklyn"/"The Bad Guys") provides another great score, but it’s all set dressing on a film one never really connects with in a meaning way.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: By some miracle, wasting your time may be the least of the director’s crimes against humanity.
reviews.author: Jonathan Sim

reviews.text: A rather boring film that, behind the curtain of political conspiracies, mixes genres uselessly and seems to be the product of a disjointed assemblage at the service of seedy characters who only spend their time talking nonsense. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: An overstuffed, muddled, historical 1930s fantasy period romantic comedy-thriller that dazzles.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: Russell spins a madcap saga that doesn’t achieve the blissful absurdity of the Coen Brothers or the gripping intrigue of Hitchcock, but instead concludes on a tender, heartfelt note...
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: A monumental waste of time and talent. One of the worst films of year. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nestor Bentancor

reviews.text: Besides protracted, the film remains too derivative, superficial, and humorless to produce an acceptable outcome.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Credit to David O. Russell for trying to make a movie, Amsterdam, that’s unique and compelling. He didn’t really succeed, but at least he tried.
reviews.author: Eileen Jones

reviews.text: It focuses attention on an important historical episode, the effort by elements in the ruling class to organize a coup in 1933–34 against Franklin D. Roosevelt, but severely fails in its treatment of the event as well as its contemporary significance.
reviews.author: David Walsh

reviews.text: It takes well over an hour before Amsterdam decides what it wants to be and, by that time, viewers may be exasperated by the film’s quirkiness and exhausted by its meandering, unfocused storyline.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: Russell has done some great world-building here — as has his crew, in a more literal sense — but he overindulges in that world. Perhaps there’s no one in the allegedly megalomaniacal auteur’s sphere who’s willing to tell him no.
reviews.author: D. Patrick Rodgers

reviews.text: For those who think more is more... and better. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Antonio Trashorras

reviews.text: Everything is senseless. The script, the direction, the mellifluous performances. If this is what North American auteur cinema has to bring, it is doomed. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: ... at times exhausting, offers small sparks without quite lighting up the flame of entertainment. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: A mixed experience, replete with stellar acting talent, but the moments of lacklustre writing and uncertain direction end on an awkward note
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: Gives us a beautiful reflection on the value of friendship, love, and patriotism. Its foundation stone brings us closer to principles that we tend to forget in the present: the beauty that lies in the ugly and broken [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Luis Bond

reviews.text: A film in which it is not known if the grotesque is intended or accidental.
reviews.author: Rubén Romero Santos

reviews.text: Amsterdam makes a great tourist destination but its promise fades in David O. Russell’s newest movie.
reviews.author: Robin Holabird

reviews.text: Scenes drag on. Characters seem to be in different movies. The film looks terrific because of Judy Becker’s superior production values, but good grief, where are we headed?
reviews.author: Michael Calleri

reviews.text: Many interesting characters get waylaid en route to the point.
reviews.author: Derek Sante

reviews.text: It’s apparent from the early minutes of Amsterdam — a comedic mystery thriller that blends fascinating fact with rather lackluster fiction — that the divisive filmmaker’s latest likely will never come together.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: You search for what's right with this movie and end up with a list of what's not.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: The cinematic equivalent of an old person telling you a story from their past, and you just nod along for what seems like forever, waiting for it to go somewhere or get interesting.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: ...increasingly endless and flat-out incoherent...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: A nimbly executed variety hour.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: Like a sloppy guy at a bar telling a farfetched tale
reviews.author: Jordan Hoffman

reviews.text: There are at least half a dozen good ideas lurking within Amsterdam, but they all struggle for breathing room. Unleashing all his ideas on the screen results in Russell’s most vibrant film in years, but also his most inconsistent.
reviews.author: Victoria Luxford

reviews.text: Russell wants to rightly tackle the rise of fascism in American politics & corporations, but like too many in the media never finds the right tone to keep us engaged in the danger, instead floundering with a weak comedic tone and a lack of proper urgency.
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: Amsterdam transforms a nightmare into a dark comedy -- at times brilliant, at times inarticulate -- greatly benefitted by the notable performances that manage to save the ship from wreckage. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Bonfil

reviews.text: Despite the frenetic, anarchic energy that carries the film along, there is loads of charm.
reviews.author: Candice McMillan

reviews.text: There's little faulting the spirited actors circling around Bale, Washington and Robbie — Malek, Saldana, Riseborough and De Niro especially — or that lead threesome.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: The kind of misfire that only talented people could make.
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: Wildly ambitious and thoroughly complex, this sprawling David O. Russell period piece has a thick, gummy quality as if it were made in a vacuum, yet it's too relevant to entirely dismiss.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: It's incredibly ambitious, I'll give it that, but it's an absolute mess.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: Hollywood's sickening obsession with fascism has found a new victim in David O. Russell. [Full review in Spanish].
reviews.author: Julio Fernando Navas

reviews.text: Disjointed and paced too slowly, it uses a convoluted plot to deliver a message that’s very simple
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: This is not a cohesive plot.
reviews.author: Marie Asner

reviews.text: Stylish and evocative, this ambitious if overwrought throwback playfully spins a multilayered story with breezy efficiency, even if it lacks much background depth and relevant context.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: This murder mystery is a curious history lesson that comes without expecting us to know the dates or names, but exposing what we did and didn't learn and that might be the biggest mystery of all.
reviews.author: Jana Monji

reviews.text: David O. Russell's starry misfire...
reviews.author: Dennis Harvey

reviews.text: ...a flawed, subversive, and sometimes beautiful viewing experience.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: What we get from director-writer David O. Russell two movies/stories going on and one is more interesting than the other. Unfortunately, the interesting part is not the main story.
reviews.author: Robin Clifford

reviews.text: It's an intermittently entertaining but rather frustrating film that could have benefited from a little more focus.
reviews.author: Patrick Cremona

reviews.text: You might be pleasantly surprised by Amsterdam. It’s an old school dark comedy with an uber-talented cast that all work together to create an enjoyable bit of cinematic escapism.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: What was once tumultuous in Russell’s work has now become tedious, resulting in a film about the lingering effects of the wars of our past and the wars to come that’s too caught up in its own internal combat to discover the compatibility that it seeks...
reviews.author: Will Ashton

reviews.text: Alas, a starry guest list is one thing, a memorable party is another, and Russell’s tired and tiresome display is all set-up and no pay-off.
reviews.author: Chris Wasser

reviews.text: The buddy bond that Bale and Washington forge goes a long way to holding Amsterdam together, and Robbie’s free-spirited third cements it.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: David O Russell keeps the tone light while punching bigger themes, so it feels somewhat uneven as the details begin to emerge. But the friendships at the centre are beautifully played, and the twisty narrative is both pointed and entertaining.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Amsterdam would appear to be a veiled warning to America about fascism. Bale is funny and Robbie's star wattage keeps it afloat, but if I hadn't been trapped in a movie theater, I would have hit pause and started looking for something more stimulating.
reviews.author: Mark Jackson

reviews.text: Russell’s new film, Amsterdam, feels like the weaknesses underlying all of his earlier works laid bare, fully exposed, without good ideas to hide behind because, quite frankly, there aren’t any real ideas here to speak of.
reviews.author: Melanie Fischer

reviews.text: it should have just focused on the 3 friends but instead we get introduced to 2 dozen or so characters all with their own plotlines and eccentricities until it becomes too much.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: The worst sin a movie can commit is to be boring. The second worst sin is to be confusing. Amsterdam commits both sins.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The idea of the story got too big... and he [David O. Russell] overstuffed it.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: Amsterdam is able to bring a few performances to the table that are worthy of raving about, but the overall experience is disappointing. The tone is all over the place, and the story feels disjointed.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: At once pretentious and self-important but also snarky and nearly nonsensical, ‘Amsterdam’ is one of the least pleasant, most inaccessible movies of the year.
reviews.author: Neal Pollack

reviews.text: Somewhere along the way the story gets lost in a sluggish haze.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: May “Amsterdam” ’s melodramatic sentimentality be forgiven; not many films of such exuberance, since the time of Chaplin, have been fuelled by such rage.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: If [Russell] had found his old screwball energy, he might have made his film’s multiple strands and cryptic plot gel together. Just as importantly, Amsterdam would have been a good deal funnier.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: Amsterdam is not a bad film by any means, as it remains watchable due to its appreciated efforts from the cast and crew. The film just needed a good captain to guide the ship from going overboard. Unfortunately, David O. Russell is not that person.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: A meandering, utterly inconsistent murder mystery bloated with an excess of quirkiness that squanders an all-star cast. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: It’s a shaggy dog story in the classic sense, only the dog in question is a bit of a mutt.
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: Amsterdam doesn’t match Russell’s best work...sure, the performances can be tasty but this oddly realized movie often has the feel of an interesting fellow who answers the doorbell without first pulling himself together.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: Despite its ambitions (and spectacular cast) the film loses itself in its own indulgences. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Iván Morales

reviews.text: Despite Russell’s being our cleverest satirist, Amsterdam succumbs to the worst ideas now afflicting our nation. Wonderfully humane as it is, Amsterdam can’t surmount the prevailing sense of failure.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: Russell’s conclusions are maudlin, but also curiously effective -- the film’s broad earnestness and sappy entreaties, prove hard to dismiss.
reviews.author: Richard Lawson

reviews.text: The all-star cast talks, talks & talks some more within a murder mystery that is so convoluted the audience (represented by me) could care less about what was going on. Chris Rock acts like Chris Rock in 1930s America. Right. A lead balloon in quicksand.
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: Though it falters in many major ways, David O. Russell’s not especially funny, tense or well-acted spiritual sequel to American Hustle is carried by an enviable cast and benign, off-kilter charm.
reviews.author: Nick Hasted

reviews.text: ...like a Wes Anderson movie without the clockwork precision and sure command of tone.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: One of its basic premises, that rich and powerful people may be relied upon to act in their own interests and against those of the wider public, should not be hard to sell
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: You do have to pay attention, as every new twist takes you in a different direction.  That being said, head to the nearest cinema and book a ticket to “Amsterdam.”
reviews.author: Michael A. Smith

reviews.text: Although the story seems to go around in circles, the trio are entertaining and quirky enough to help you forget the incoherent plot. Bale steals the show as a fun but peculiar character.
reviews.author: Lupe Rodriguez Haas

reviews.text: Behind the high energy and flashy cast, there's a shocking lack of emotional depth — like a performer giving us jazz hands paired with a vacant stare.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: It's too long, and moves to slowly but the dialogue is funny, and the cast is terrific especially Margot Robbie. I had a good time. It's an old-fashioned entertaining Hollywood farce with friendship at the core and support for our veterans.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: In the same way that its bloated cast becomes a distraction which takes you out of the story, Amsterdam is unnecessarily convoluted, twisting its confusing narrative into a cobra knot.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: It’s on the lower end of Russell’s filmography in terms of memorability, but is handled with such a light, circusy touch that it’s not a bad way to kill a few hours.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: Not even its top-notch cast is able to redeem this discordant film whose important message gets lost in the chaos. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Rene Sanchez

reviews.text: Russell’s showy directorial pizzazz is very much in evidence, but there’s an edge of desperation to the chunks of exposition that dam the flow of this already meandering tale.
reviews.author: Wendy Ide

reviews.text: ...succeeds only at finding incoherence.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: I admit, I fell for this messy, off-beat extravaganza. And I think it has a lot more to say than some may give it credit for.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Racism, antisemitism, fascism, a seriously stern Robert De Niro, as an angry Marine General, and the very good Margot Robbie also play key roles in a crowded screenplay that misses more than it hits.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: David O. Russell’s “Amsterdam” is a sophisticated, three-stooge-like mystery that’s ultimately a love letter to veterans.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: As it accumulates running time (and characters and plot points), Amsterdam starts to get exhausting when it should perhaps feel liberating or intoxicating.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: For all its tepidness Amsterdam does grasp at bigger ideas .... That it feels like a piecemeal film made up of dozens of other films talking points and premises is precisely what cements its unremarkability, what a pity.
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: What a cast and what an unfortunate use and waste of their talent. Writer/Director, David O. Russell makes this 1930’s murder mystery a long, rambling buddy film, but the disjointed script takes way too long to build up to the climax.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: The cherry on top of this film is the camaraderie between the characters portrayed by Bale, Washington, and Robbie.  We see the beginnings of the friendship and the love between them, and then seeing them become crime sleuths is quite amusing.
reviews.author: Sarah Ksiazek

reviews.text: Russell has actually crafted what at its core is a fundamentally simple story designed to push an overt message, before bogging it down in quirky supporting characters and unnecessary detours.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: The excellent cast cannot overcome the convoluted script that has a good message but lacks real focus.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: Jaw-droppingly terrible, interminably dull...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Russell, to his everlasting credit, has made a film in which having cockeyed optimism, at this moment in the world, somehow feels like a radical act.
reviews.author: David Fear

reviews.text: The final voiceover smacks the audience over the head with The Point of the film so aggressively, it seems that Russell genuinely didn’t think anyone would be able to work it out for themselves.
reviews.author: Mary Siroky

reviews.text: Amsterdam opens with the statement, “A lot of this really happened.” But audiences who sit through this confused mess of a movie aren’t going to know which parts are fact and which parts are fiction. Also, they’re unlikely to care.
reviews.author: Collin Garbarino

reviews.text: From Oscar-winning showman David O. Russell, 64, there's so much razzmatazz, artistry and comedic snap -- yet the antic pastiche lacks a satisfying mystery plot and, sadly, is less than the sum of its amazing performances.
reviews.author: Thelma Adams

reviews.text: With its overblown stylings, and wavy, melodramatic tone, it's as if we're watching the feature debut of Max Fischer, the precocious teenager from Wes Anderson's "Rushmore." That's not intended as a compliment.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: [The] film that seems to aspire to the screwball of Preston Sturges. But the pace is too slow for that, the jokes too laboured, and while there are some fine comic performances, Amsterdam is muddled in its intentions.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: How five-time Oscar nominee David O. Russell, director and writer of “Amsterdam,” could squander such a star-studded award-winning cast in one of the most eagerly anticipated fall releases is more of a mystery than this convoluted period piece.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Terribly written by Russell and obtusely edited (huge gaps between lines)... It’s mostly an endurance test. But, wow, those faces.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Russell's misstep with Amsterdam is as unexpected as it is shocking.
reviews.author: Frank Wilkins

reviews.text: A lot of interesting, colorful pieces that don't really fit together in this latest fizzy fizzle from David O. Russell.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: Overwrought and mostly exposition, "Amsterdam" is a beautiful corpse. Talented ensemble cast wasted.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: It is an inspiring movie, it gives you a breather and allows for the audience to forgive the "mistunes" and its lack of rhythm. At the end tells an untold story and as all those dark war stories, is worth to be told.. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Laura Hiros

reviews.text: Only in its milder moments, when Russell is not trying too hard to be madcap, or to badger us with dark political portents, does “Amsterdam” stir and convince.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: A three-headed showcase of Christian Bale, John David Washington, and Margot Robbie drives the narrative. Sadly, a mess of a screenplay sinks the film early and continues to distract throughout.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: It feels as though the entire script were constructed from a rather rowdy game of Cards Against Humanity.
reviews.author: Karen M. Peterson

reviews.text: Unfortunately, the movie is bad.
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: What Amsterdam lacks in tight storytelling, it more than makes up for in exuberant, happy-go-lucky spirit.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: Amsterdam is a quirky, convoluted, comedic thriller with a game cast of A-listers, most of them giving intriguing performances that are refreshingly unlike anything we've seen from them before.
reviews.author: Lisa Johnson Mandell

reviews.text: The effect is one of distance; Russell may want us to love these characters and be invested in the bigger story they're telling, but he lets his own worst habits get in the way.
reviews.author: Don Kaye

reviews.text: Simultaneously overstuffed and undernourished, frantic and meandering, Amsterdam is one big, star-studded, hot mess of a movie.
reviews.author: Christy Lemire

reviews.text: Almost enough moving pieces to distract from what’s by far the messiest script of Russell’s illustrious career.
reviews.author: Edwin Arnaudin

reviews.text: Pills and perversity have always brought out the best in Russell.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: Amsterdam has all the elements of O. Russell’s previous works with an A-list cast and intriguing story. Unfortunately that’s about all the film has going for it. A lifeless script and average direction struggles to make even the brightest of stars shine.
reviews.author: Matt Rodriguez

reviews.text: The frequently boring and muddled Amsterdam has many big-name stars, but this misguided drama just adds up to a lot of posturing and hot air. The filmmakers cared more about wrangling celebrities into the cast than crafting a story worthy of this talent.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: The film is stunningly shot by Emmanuel Lubezki, who has the camera revel in the zaniness. The film moves swiftly, and, in the end, we are left with heady themes about how history seems to keep repeating itself…
reviews.author: Frank J. Avella

reviews.text: David O. Russell’s strands an A-list cast —Bale! Robbie! Washington! De Niro!— in a pokey and problematic mystery romp. You can feel Russell’s cage-rattling intensity, but only in fits and starts as the convoluted conspiracy plot goes out in a fizzle.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: A big, hammy mess of a movie.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Despite the dense procedural and political details, the simple pleasure of two stars doing what only they can do best is what finally makes Amsterdam old-fashioned in the way Russell intended all along.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: The kind of film in which those in it seem to be having a bigger hoot than those of us watching, making it a waste not just of a tip-top cast, but also of a cracking yarn.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: Will leave you not giving a Dam.
reviews.author: Dulcie Pearce

reviews.text: Gorgeous cinematography from Emmanuel Lubezki, Judy Becker’s excellent production design, and Albert Wolsky’s fabulous costumes add to the frustration. A good-looking waste, but a waste nonetheless.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: The actors are killing it - there was never a dull moment hanging with them. And the mystery works well.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: By the time the screenplay arrives at a real-life historical event of political importance ... whatever life the actors try to bring to this material has been drained.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Though Bale’s 1933 face is a wreck, filled with scars and with that missing eye, the story bounces along with peppy abandon, highlighting serious issues like love, racism, and greed without sacrificing panache. But then the speechifying begins . . .
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Okay, but not among the filmmaker's best.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Perhaps O. Russell should start resharpening his storytelling craft instead of just casting big stars. At the end of the day, it's the story that ought to be the star of the movie.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Ambitious, stimulating, and inspirational, David O. Russell’s “Amsterdam” takes a little-known historic event and uses it as the basis for a seemingly convoluted mystery that winds up being a paean to friendship and patriotism.
reviews.author: Charles Koplinski

reviews.text: “Amsterdam” tries to be too much and winds up not being enough.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: The film purports to be a screwball mystery while delivering none of the charms that a film like that should offer its audience.
reviews.author: Steve Katz

reviews.text: David O. Russell's latest film is notably far from his best work, yet manages to be mostly enjoyable thanks to its incredible cast, high production value and quirky tone. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: David O. Russell’s new film, “Amsterdam” has a powerhouse cast, a wisp of a true story and a wildly uneven and overly complicated script. The results are, therefore, messy and mixed.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: A zany farce with a sweet core that it takes a lot of work to unearth, "Amsterdam" is overcomplicated and often confounding but finds redemption in its resolution.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: In the film’s roundabout way that owes much to Chinatown (1974), Amsterdam begins with a simple investigation and unfolds into an intricate story about power and wealth.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: To describe Amsterdam as an unfunny comedy would be unfair, because it’s so much more than that. It’s also a non-thrilling thriller and a not particularly mysterious mystery.
reviews.author: Kyle Smith

reviews.text: It sometimes isn’t as funny as it’s trying to be in the lighter sections, and occasionally bypasses depth and hits preachy when it has something to say. This makes for a bit of a bumpy ride, though it’s more or less entertaining.
reviews.author: Abbie Bernstein

reviews.text: The limp, negligible result is an unwelcome reminder that even talented filmmakers can and will stumble.
reviews.author: Mel Valentin

reviews.text: An overlong, overstuffed windup that amounts to very little.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: Despite its noble intentions, Amsterdam is uneven and wastes a stellar cast.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: Russell's moral indignation spins the movie away from messy, spirited caper and toward an astonishingly corny final act.
reviews.author: Luke Goodsell

reviews.text: I’m compelled to admit that Amsterdam is done in by its flaws in conception and execution.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: What recommends Amsterdam, despite its considerable problems, is its social critique of racism and anti-Semitism and its democratic message still relevant today.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: It's overlong and a bit too thrilled with its own madcap vibe, but it has some great scenes, life wisdom to cherish and a grandstand finish where the bravura is secondary to the point that Russell is making.
reviews.author: Harry Guerin

reviews.text: Amsterdam uses the trick of "true events" as an alibi more so than a validation. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Paula Vázquez Prieto

reviews.text: There’s plenty of tragedy here -- along with ignorance, racism and murderous malice -- but the glue that binds the narrative together and makes it work is Russell’s sense of fun.
reviews.author: Sandra Hall

reviews.text: Rarely have so many stars labored to so little effect as they do in "Amsterdam."
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Amsterdam draws on its expert cast to craft a biting social and political commentary filled with pointed humor but is ultimately hampered by obvious story choices, repetitive scenes, strange cast direction, and an ending that insults the audience.
reviews.author: Chris Joyce

reviews.text: The central performances are charming, and stretches of the film are enjoyable. Everything looks stylish and wonderful, and everyone has nice hair... The thing is, there is a great film in here fighting to get out, but it’s drowned out by manic plotting.
reviews.author: Jessie Thompson

reviews.text: Amsterdam’s three leads – individually charismatic performers all – collectively can’t sell the film’s sentimental, facile idea that love beats all, even those pesky fascists.
reviews.author: Kimberley Jones

reviews.text: For much of “Amsterdam,” the latest David O. Russell Experience, the movie enjoyably zigs and zags, rushing here and there, though sometimes also just spinning in place.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Christian Bale, Margot Robbie, and John David Washington have fantastic chemistry but they get buried under the weight of a script that suffocates the humanity of their story.
reviews.author: Tara Bennett

reviews.text: A satire sprinkled with verbal and physical gags, and the well-thought out plot twists are even better executed
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: What a mess.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: It’s part comedy, part mystery, part social commentary, all rolled into one, but it needed to be funnier, more thrilling, and less hectoring. It’s a noble effort, it’s also one of the bigger missed opportunities of 2022.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Even with a lot of outstanding components, something feels off about the final product.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: Robbie is incredibly talented and so strikingly beautiful that she dominates every scene she is in, even to the point of eclipsing the equally talented and beautiful, Taylor-Joy,
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Kind of a mess, but in many respects a quite enjoyable one...it offers enough incidental pleasures along the way to put it—almost—into the plus column.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: The production is first rate, from Academy Award nominated director David O. Russell, to the a-list cast to the ambitious script that links events of the past to today’s headlines. But the film is definitely less than the sum of its parts.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: David O. Russell’s “Amsterdam” is a shaggy dog story that’s more like a dog’s breakfast.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: It’s a blundering mess of a movie, but an endearing one.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: It’s part “JFK,” part “The Big Lebowski,” and the mix doesn’t work.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Too often the film seems to be moving sideways, or skipping like a needle on an old LP.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: It starts out confusingly, and thuds for a while toward the end. Otherwise, it’s airborne and just so, like a Wes Anderson movie with muscles and actual human emotion.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: Very gradually the discursive nature of the narrative coalesces into a fairly conventional plot-driven yarn...Fans of Russell, though arguably few else, will forgive the film’s as-you-please pacing and relish the rich performances and production values.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Russell doesn't seem to have made up his mind in which genre making Amsterdam; satire, crime, drama, suspense, noir, or comedy, cramming it all together in a recipe whose ingredients just don't mix. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Rivera Rubio

reviews.text: A painfully dull, bloated and clunky mess that's neither fun, suspenseful or intriguing. It's ultimately less than the sum of its parts.
reviews.author: Avi Offer

reviews.text: I can’t deny that certain moving parts piqued my interest, but all too often did they come to a halt, with even such star wattage unable to blindingly distract from its messy assemblage.
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: This is a complex, character-driven conspiracy tale that’s full of twists and turns, memorable moments and more than one message that should resonate with modern-day audiences.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: If Amsterdam believes anything, it’s that democracy is defined by the seemingly small things that make a human being an individual, absurd as they may be.
reviews.author: Bennett Campbell Ferguson

reviews.text: This true-crime period comedy romance adventure with its mannered wackiness and empty caricatures is a misfire, nothing like the 2013 true-crime period caper American Hustle.
reviews.author: Whang Yee Ling

reviews.text: The new movie “Amsterdam” has been shrouded in secrecy for months. We now know why — it’s unwatchable.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: “Amsterdam” is proof that just because you have all the right pieces in place, it’s still possible to screw it up.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: The star-studded whodunnit isn’t as clever as it thinks it is.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: On the level of that period gangster movie Ben Affleck directed in Florida with the hats. Do you dearly hope that a fever dream by a fiscally empowered filmmaker is filled with cacophonous magic rather than half-waking sludge? “Amsterdam” will fail you.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Unfocused but entertaining. Has a very odd tone where it veers from slapstick humor to ultraviolence in seconds.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: “Amsterdam” only fitfully locates the moment-to-moment comic verve — or the bittersweet sense of longing — that would give these characters and their farcical shenanigans the deeper human resonance it’s clearly aiming for.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: David O. Russell knows what he's trying to say but can't choose the genre or tone of his film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Benjamín Harguindey

reviews.text: This meandering mess boasts an A-list cast that’s given the extraordinary task of attempting to pull together the scattered shards of a plot. Spoiler alert: They’re only sporadically successful.
reviews.author: Rebecca Murray

reviews.text: Welcome to Amsterdam, writer and director David O. Russell’s answer to the question: Can some of the top actors in the world mange to elevate poor material? The answer is a dull no. It becomes a slaughterhouse.
reviews.author: Mark Kennedy

reviews.text: A highly pedigreed film that’s a floundering misfire.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: One of the most perfectly unremarkable, utterly average movies I can recall.
reviews.author: Sean Collier

reviews.text: the minute you start to think too much about it, even while watching it, everything about it melts away like cotton candy exposed to moisture.
reviews.author: Ryan Silberstein

reviews.text: If Russell's intent was to direct a film that runs 134 minutes and feels the length of a TV miniseries, then allow me to be the first to congratulate him on a job well done.
reviews.author: Brent Hankins

reviews.text: The star wattage is blinding, but the film fizzles out.
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: This mostly made-up period frolic has a kernel of harsh historical truth at the center of its merrily crowded, retro-rollicking tale of friendship, bonds that last a lifetime and places in the heart.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: The central trio deliver big, broad, movie-star performances that carry us along so that Russell can sneak in more serious points about the shameful neglect of those on the margins.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Ultimately, Amsterdam has big issues with immersion and cohesion, making it a bit clunky, but the underlying tale and never-ending twists salvage the film enough to still be an unmissable watch.
reviews.author: Samantha Leathers

reviews.text: The movie’s saving grace is its contagious passion, and Russell’s unavoidably true thesis is that, as historical loops go, the one we’re in right now a doozy.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: If you allow its turned up and persistent energy to sweep over you, and soak in the joy and righteous anger that animates its generous spirit, the end result is decidedly moving, and — at some points — even enthralling.
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: …maybe the critical masses will shrug at such a heady a mix of 30’s style and 70’s cynicism, but that doesn’t mean that you can’t enjoy Amsterdam on the sly…
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Aims to be cheeky and offbeat, but it’s exhausting instead, never finding its way as a quasi-farce about people in deep trouble.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: Director David O. Russell’s period farce has an incredibly starry cast but its plot (and logic and direction) is MIA.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: … filled with contradictions, but the biggest one is the movie itself.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: Writer/director David O. Russell’s Amsterdam is nowhere near as funny as it thinks it is
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: At 134 minutes, “Amsterdam” stumbles like a cinematic inebriate, unable to stay focused on one aspect of its story for too long.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Well, I hate to say this but after having a tough time sitting through the 134-minute slog, Amsterdam marks a rare misfire for David O. Russell.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: The basic structure of Amsterdam is a murder mystery, though there’s a fair bit of romance and even a little humour woven into the plot. There are also some lovely lines in Russell’s screenplay.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: What lingers most readily from Amsterdam are the little privileged moments.
reviews.author: Ryan Swen

reviews.text: It's a rocky, at times patience-testing ride that plays something like a screwball riff on The Plot Against America, but Amsterdam is ultimately worth the trip.
reviews.author: Jamie Graham

reviews.text: Writer/director David O. Russell...appears to have lost his mojo, his based-on-fact, history-is-repeating-itself satire about fascism, racism and anti-Semitism drowned in an overly plotted, meandering tale cluttered with too many characters.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: Russell ends up dancing around genres, not quite fitting into any particular one, lurching ahead with an intense smugness.
reviews.author: Alex Saveliev

reviews.text: While it may lean towards the bloated side with an unnecessarily long run-time, the absolutely incredible ensemble cast brings life to Russell’s most interesting work to date.
reviews.author: Kyle Wilson

reviews.text: Amsterdam is pretty good, in part because these actors are enjoying being in a period romp.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: Russell tries his hand at the Coen [brother's] misanthropic cynicism, Adam McKay's satirical spirit and Wes Anderson's stylized fables, but loses in all realms. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Amsterdam suffers from a surfeit of story detail without the vigour to whizz you through it. It has likable leads and the craft is on point, but the result, given all the talent involved, is a tonally uneasy disappointment — a romp that fails to romp.
reviews.author: Ian Freer

reviews.text: Feels like a star-studded awards bait disaster for 98% of its run time only to totally redeem itself at the last minute. In the end it's a sneaky (REALLY sneaky) profound riff on freedom, fulfillment, and fascism.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: The pals work their way through a series of mind-bogglingly tedious hijinks as the audience attempts to puzzle through why, exactly, we should care about any of this at all.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: I genuinely am not sure exactly what was going on through much of the film, other than a lot of attractive people intoning lines that they often seemed to be making up on the spot.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: “Amsterdam” is pretty much an all-star game where everybody excels at their roles and no one’s showboating.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: Amsterdam's strange circuitous journey and almost embarrassing surplus of stars never quite justifies: a whirring music-box curiosity in search of some elusive purpose, and a point.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: For a project that has so much stuff going on simultaneously, it miraculously manages to feel as if always bordering on uneventful.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: Amsterdam is for the birds. David O. Russell’s film lacks focus and lacks restraint. A self-indulgent piece of filmmaking with stale themes that no amount of production value or Hollywood stars can hide.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Enjoyable Performances Can't Save David O. Russell's Undercooked Movie
reviews.author: Jeff Ewing

reviews.text: If the triumph of evil is for good men to do nothing, the triumph of boredom is for good directors like David O. Russell to do nothing movies about evil like "Amsterdam," which ultimately amounts to a dull, disjointed allegory about altruism.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: It’s a shame that the film ultimately rang hollow, despite a lot of good effort from many involved.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Amsterdam is celebrity-obsessed, unfunny, and painfully monotonous.
reviews.author: Jeff Nelson

reviews.text: At times fun and well-made, Amsterdam's meandering plot and thinly-drawn characters bog down what could've been a zippy story of crime and friendship.
reviews.author: Rachel LaBonte

reviews.text: A dark news story from 1933 wrapped inside a screwball lark. Or maybe vice versa.
reviews.author: Danny Leigh

reviews.text: A rollicking character comedy and an almost subtle retelling of a forgotten 'past is prologue' chapter of American history. 'Amsterdam' is an acting treat and David O. Russell's best movie since 'Three Kings.'
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: The wonderful elements of Amsterdam can only do so much to glue together this faltering house of cards.
reviews.author: Aurora Amidon

reviews.text: What remains when Amsterdam grinds to a halting conclusion is a work of poor imitation, a cinematic con that fails to convince us it's actually any good as a film or worth even a moment of time taken seriously.
reviews.author: Chase Hutchinson

reviews.text: Aside from a good day at the office for Bale, there's not much to love from Amsterdam. It's ultimately a waste of one of the most impressive ensembles in recent memory, and markets itself as far more interesting than it actually is.
reviews.author: Liam Crowley

reviews.text: Despite Russell’s penchant for comedic chaos, Amsterdam is best when simplified to the trio of best friends at its core.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Amsterdam convolutes a murder mystery, forbidden love story, and fascist attempted coup in 1930s New York. David O. Russell gets humor and creativity points but fails dramatically at pacing. Amsterdam's long runtime drips like molasses going backwards.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: [Amsterdam is] Russell’s first film where its perfunctory elements almost entirely outweigh anything resembling dramatic depth or thematic substance.
reviews.author: Paul Attard

reviews.text: The filmmaker’s cast members look as bewildered as you or I might in trying to recall the exact twists and turns of the story, or their places within it. Not that they don’t try. Lord, they try.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: The performances are not the biggest problem with the film, but they are indicative of the film’s biggest problem: “Amsterdam” involves a lot of talented people doing what they do best but merely going through the motions.
reviews.author: Dan Bayer

reviews.text: There’s enough heat to call this a lukewarm mess.
reviews.author: Jake Kring-Schreifels

reviews.text: There is far too much going on and even the incredibly talented line up of actors cannot save it. It is shame because there is something good there, underneath it all, but it is impossible to find.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: Amsterdam has a charming, shaggy-dog feel – a crazed story for a crazy world.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: Considering the talent assembled, it’s a wonder how empty and near-sighted “Amsterdam” is. Maybe they read a different script than what eventually made it to the screen.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: This madcap period piece is part murder mystery, part anti-fascist conspiracy thriller, and all-around disaster, devoid of tone, wit, or any semblance of rhythm.
reviews.author: Nick Schager

reviews.text: Amsterdam might encompass 15 years of history, straddle two continents and throw in innumerable subplots, but it becomes increasingly hard to shake the sense that you’re watching a very thin idea twiddling its thumbs.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: Although stuffed with ambition and the occasionally arresting moment, this 1930s mystery flaunts a freewheeling spirit that far outpaces its convoluted story and dramatically thin protagonists.
reviews.author: Tim Grierson

reviews.text: Amsterdam is a star-studded and messy affair that provides a decent amount of enjoyment.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Russell, as I said, has made many really great films. His heart is always in the right place...Somehow this massive carnival of ideas got away from him
reviews.author: Roger Friedman

reviews.text: An epic, sprawling and ambitious fable, it's like a whimsical fairytale about the insidiousness of creeping authoritarianism and stopping a fascistic plot against America.
reviews.author: Rodrigo Perez

reviews.text: There are some very good performances, and Washington has taken another step towards A-lister greatness.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: A wildly over-cranked plea to “protect kindness” that rings every bit as forced and hollow as you might expect from someone with such a pronounced reputation for killing it himself.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: A must-see for smart adult audiences.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: Can any film be called satisfying when the storytelling is so convoluted it takes an hour or more to settle on the kind of story it wants to tell, let alone a cohesive tone in which to tell it?
reviews.author: David Rooney

reviews.text: Even though this oddball ensemble boasts intelligent ideas and a smorgasbord of against-type performances from A-list names, “Amsterdam” amounts to less than the sum of its parts.
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: No amount of star wattage can lift this flat, unfunny genre-fluid whatsit from its performative stumbling toward contemporary relevance.
reviews.author: Robert Abele

synopsis: In 1933 three close friends find themselves at the center of one of the most shocking secret plots in American history.
